# macosdefaults_preference (Resource)

Manages one preference key in one domain, as `defaults write` would set it.

The property list type is inferred from `value`: strings, bools, whole numbers (`integer`), fractional numbers (`float`), lists (`array`) and maps or objects (`dict`), recursively. Set `type` to override the inferred type of the top-level value: `float` for a whole number an app expects as a real, `date` for an RFC 3339 string, or `data` for a base64 string.

Changes made outside Terraform (in System Settings, or by the app) show up as drift. A boolean stored by the app as the integer 1 or 0 counts as unchanged.

Destroying the resource deletes the key, so the app goes back to its built-in default. The rest of the domain is never touched. The provider doesn't restart apps; many only read preferences at launch.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Booleans, numbers and strings infer their plist type.
resource "macosdefaults_preference" "dock_autohide" {
  domain = "com.apple.dock"
  key    = "autohide"
  value  = true
}

resource "macosdefaults_preference" "key_repeat" {
  domain = "NSGlobalDomain"
  key    = "KeyRepeat"
  value  = 2
}

resource "macosdefaults_preference" "screenshot_location" {
  domain = "com.apple.screencapture"
  key    = "location"
  value  = pathexpand("~/Pictures/Screenshots") # defaults doesn't expand ~
}

# Override inference when an app stores a whole number as a real.
resource "macosdefaults_preference" "dock_tilesize" {
  domain = "com.apple.dock"
  key    = "tilesize"
  value  = 48
  type   = "float"
}

# Lists and maps become arrays and dicts, nested as deeply as needed.
resource "macosdefaults_preference" "finder_view_settings" {
  domain = "com.apple.finder"
  key    = "FXInfoPanesExpanded"
  value = {
    General  = true
    MetaData = false
    Preview  = false
  }
}

# Per-machine (ByHost) preferences.
resource "macosdefaults_preference" "battery_percentage" {
  domain = "com.apple.controlcenter"
  key    = "BatteryShowPercentage"
  value  = true
  scope  = "current_host"
}

# Many apps only read preferences at launch.
resource "terraform_data" "restart_dock" {
  triggers_replace = [
    macosdefaults_preference.dock_autohide.value,
    macosdefaults_preference.dock_tilesize.value,
  ]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "killall Dock"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `domain` (String) Preference domain, usually an app's bundle identifier (`com.apple.dock`), or `NSGlobalDomain` for settings shared by every app. Names must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and spaces; aliases such as `-g` and `.GlobalPreferences`, and file paths, aren't accepted. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `key` (String) Preference key within the domain. Any non-empty name works, except one starting with `-` or containing control characters. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `value` (Dynamic) The value to store: a string, bool, number, list or map, nested as deeply as needed. Nulls can't be stored. Dates and data need `type`.

### Optional

- `scope` (String) Which preferences to use: `user` for the current user's preferences, `current_host` for the current user's preferences on this Mac only (`defaults -currentHost`), or `system` for machine-wide preferences in `/Library/Preferences`. `system` requires running Terraform as root, and the other scopes require *not* running as root. Defaults to the provider's `scope`. Changing the effective scope (here or on the provider) replaces the resource.
- `type` (String) Property list type: one of `string`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `data`, `array` or `dict`. Inferred from `value` when unset; when set, it must fit `value` (a number for `integer` or `float`, an RFC 3339 string with whole seconds for `date`, a base64 string for `data`).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<scope>/<domain>:<key>`, naming the effective scope, e.g. `user/com.apple.dock:autohide`. Usable as an import ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <scope>/<domain>:<key>, matching the resource's id
terraform import macosdefaults_preference.battery_percentage 'current_host/com.apple.controlcenter:BatteryShowPercentage'

# <domain>:<key> uses the provider's default scope
terraform import macosdefaults_preference.dock_autohide 'com.apple.dock:autohide'
```
